canonical_name: Bishop's rational-approximation theorem family (exact Theorem 4 encoding open)
literal_source_claim_en: A necessary and sufficient condition for rational approximation.
source_attribution: Errett Bishop, 1959 (catalog metadata only; no citation supplied)
candidate_statement_family_not_credited: For a compact subset C of the complex plane with empty interior, Bishop's 1959 Theorem 4 relates universal uniform approximation on C by rational functions with poles off C to conditions involving the minimal boundary M of the corresponding closed separating algebra, real-part approximation, strong peak points, and planar measure zero of C minus M.
statement_blocker: The uncited catalog gloss closely matches Bishop 1959, Theorem 4, but it does not select that source or one canonical equivalence, and it omits the definitions of the rational-function algebra, controlled poles, uniform closure, minimal boundary, real-part algebra, peak set, planar measure and boundary cases. The source is a two-page announcement rather than the located full proof. An immutable definition-complete source and independent review must approve the exact claim before Lean elaboration.
domain_and_universes: Prospective compact set C in the complex plane, the subtype C with its compact metric topology, complex- and real-valued continuous maps on C, rational functions with poles outside C, and planar measure. Exact universes, representations, topology and measure instances remain open.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not select universal rational approximation iff minimal boundary equals C, iff the complement has planar measure zero, or Bishop's complete four-way equivalence including real-part approximation.
